z-m-27-01.title: How many ways dey to hand out 6 candies?
z-m-27-01.topic: The number of ways to hand out candies: whether candies na told apart and whether empty hands na allowed
z-m-27-01.goal: Realize that the sentence 'the number of ways to hand out' alone does not fix a single answer, and rewrite the problem by stating for yourself the conditions needed to decide the answer (whether candies na told apart, whether empty hands na allowed).
z-m-27-01.material: We want to hand out all 6 candies to three people, 갑, 을, and 병. 갑, 을, and 병 have fixed names, so they na different people. Ways of handing out candies na counted by the result 'who received what.' If the result is the same, it is the same way, and order of giving candies is not counted. The problem is just one sentence. "How many ways dey to hand out 6 candies to three people?"
z-m-27-01.thinking.0: Decide if information enough before finding answer
z-m-27-01.thinking.1: Predict how number of cases go change when conditions change
z-m-27-01.thinking.2: Checking by building cases whose conditions na fixed
z-m-27-01.thinking.3: Rewrite unclear problem so e get one answer
z-m-27-01.prereq.0: Write cases as ordered pairs and list all of dem without missing any
z-m-27-01.prereq.1: The product rule and sum rule (level of the early part of the 'counting cases' unit in high school Common Mathematics)
z-m-27-01.prereq.2: H2 for school-level assignment na only difficulty label for this plan, e no assign school grade. Assume say basic ideas of counting cases unit don learn already.
z-m-27-01.s.s1.prompt: For this one sentence to have only one answer, wetin else we must know? Choose all wey apply.
z-m-27-01.s.s1.hint.0: Separate, as if drawing a line, the conditions already written in the problem text from the conditions that na not written.
z-m-27-01.s.s1.hint.1: Fix one count for (갑, 을, 병) so that the result stays the same, and think about which condition, if changed, would make that result different or impossible.
z-m-27-01.s.s1.o.a: The ages of the three people 갑, 을, and 병
z-m-27-01.s.s1.r.a: Age has nothing to do with how many ways there na to divide. Think about which information changes the way of counting.
z-m-27-01.s.s1.o.b: Whether the 6 candies na told apart from each other
z-m-27-01.s.s1.r.b: You noticed that depending on whether the candies na told apart, even the same distribution of numbers can be counted as different ways.
z-m-27-01.s.s1.o.c: Whether candies na given one at a time in turn or all at once
z-m-27-01.s.s1.r.c: Dem set this problem to count result only, no be order of giving. Na fixed condition already.
z-m-27-01.s.s1.o.d: Whether e dey okay if one of three people no get candy at all
z-m-27-01.s.s1.r.d: You noticed that whether the cases where someone receives 0 na included changes the very list of possible cases.
z-m-27-01.s.s1.o.e: Whether 갑, 을, and 병 na different people
z-m-27-01.s.s1.r.e: E already say dem get fixed names. Separate information wey dem give from wetin missing.
z-m-27-01.s.s1.explain: There na two pieces of missing information. Depending on whether the candies na told apart, even when the numbers na the same, like (갑 4, 을 1, 병 1), it becomes a different way if the candies received na different. Also, the possible cases change depending on whether an empty hand is allowed. That the people na told apart and that the order of giving is not counted have already been given.
z-m-27-01.s.s2.prompt: Let's fix the case where all 6 candies na the same kind and all three people receive at least 1 each. Enter 6 different ways. (the number 갑 receives is a, the number 을 receives is b, the number 병 receives is c)
z-m-27-01.s.s2.hint.0: First choose number one person receive, then check wetin sum for other two people must be.
z-m-27-01.s.s2.hint.1: (4,1,1) and (1,4,1) na same way? Check against problem rule say “if result same, na same way.”
z-m-27-01.s.s2.ok.c1: All three people get at least 1.
z-m-27-01.s.s2.fail.c1: All 3 people must get at least 1 each.
z-m-27-01.s.s2.ok.c2: Candy no fit divide, so numbers na integers.
z-m-27-01.s.s2.fail.c3: Total candy the 3 people receive must be 6.
z-m-27-01.s.s2.explain: With this condition, total 10 ways dey. (1,1,4), (1,4,1), and (4,1,1) count as different because different person get 4 candy. This happen because we distinguish the 3 people. Even same number set (1,2,3) get 6 arrangements depending who receive how much.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.prompt: Now assume the 6 candies na all different flavours, and person fit get none. Compna with dividing candies of the same kind with empty hands allowed (28 ways), wetin happen to number of ways?
z-m-27-01.s.s3.hint.0: Choose one distribution from same-kind case, (4,1,1), and count how many ways e split when the candies na told apart.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.hint.1: Think choose who get each candy one after another, 'which of the three people gets it,' and count how many choices.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.o.a: E reduce. Because we distinguish the candies, condition stricter.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.r.a: Distinguishing candies no remove any distribution. Check how many ways same number distribution split.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.o.b: Same, 28 ways. Because candy and people numbers remain same.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.r.b: Even if candy and people numbers same, for same (4,1,1) distribution different if people get different candies.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.o.c: E increase. Because each distribution split in many ways.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.r.c: You notice when candies distinct, one distribution become many ways.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.o.d: We no fit know without calculating.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.r.d: You fit compna without calculate everything, by checking one distribution and how many ways e split.
z-m-27-01.s.s3.explain: If all candies different, each candy go to one of 3 people, so 3 to power 6, meaning 729 ways. Na plenty pass 28 same-kind ways. Because each of the 28 fit split into many. For example, even (4,1,1) alone split many ways depending which 4 candies 갑 get.
z-m-27-01.s.s4.prompt: Correct the first sentence and write 2 different versions with one clear answer each. You no need find answers (how many ways), but state clearly which conditions you add.
z-m-27-01.s.s4.hint.0: Set both missing details you choose before, one by one, and add dem to sentence.
z-m-27-01.s.s4.hint.1: Both versions must differ by at least one condition. Choose which condition to change and write am.
z-m-27-01.s.s4.selfAssess.0: Can you state in one line which condition different between the two interpretations you wrote?
z-m-27-01.s.s4.selfAssess.1: When you read both versions, you know if candies same or distinct?
z-m-27-01.s.s4.selfAssess.2: For each version, you know if person fit get no candy?
z-m-27-01.s.s4.model.0: Interpretation 1) All 6 candies na the same kind, and it is fine for a person to receive 0. Interpretation 2) All 6 candies na different flavors, and it is fine for a person to receive none.
z-m-27-01.s.s4.model.1: We fit write am as the number of ways to divide 6 identical candies so that all three people get at least 1 each, or as the number of ways to divide 6 candies that na told apart so that no one is left out.
z-m-27-01.s.s4.modelNote.1: This answer choose third condition combination (told apart + everyone gets 1 or more). Different combinations okay if conditions clear.
